topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causes and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Origins of Cancer: Intrinsic Mechanisms, Chance, and Epidemiological Patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine what drives cancer development across intrinsic cellular processes, random mutational events, inherited predispositions, and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Cancer Etiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on how infectious agents contribute to malignancy, detailing various oncogenic pathogens and exploring Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe specific physical, dietary, and chemical carcinogens along with their pathways of metabolic activation and direct or indirect DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on tumor promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and life-stage or tissue-specific cellular susceptibilities.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methods used to identify carcinogens and substantiate their link to cancer.

topics.label: Risk-Benefit Assessment and Lecture Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This concluding subtopic reflects on balancing exposure risks against benefits and summarizes the main themes of the lecture.
